problem: The sentence 'The industry moved to a 12 V nominal bus, which gives about 14.0 V when charged' can be read as saying the 12 V battery itself sits at 14.0 V, which contradicts the exam trap later in the chapter.
fix: The industry moved to a 12 V nominal bus; the charging system holds that bus near 14.0 V, while the battery at rest is about 12.6 V.

problem: 'Europe set Euro I to Euro V and later steps' is loose: it mixes Roman numerals with 'later steps' and skips that the Euro stages began in the early 1990s, not the 1970s where the paragraph starts.
fix: From the 1970s, governments limited carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides from petrol engines. Europe's Euro 1 stage came in the early 1990s, with tighter stages up to Euro 6; India adopted equivalent Bharat Stage norms.

problem: 'It also enables on-board diagnostics (OBD-II)' overstates the link. OBD-II existed before CAN; CAN is only one of the protocols OBD-II allows, though it became the required one for new cars in the US from 2008.
fix: It also carries the messages that on-board diagnostics (OBD-II) read; CAN became the standard OBD-II link for new cars in the US from 2008.

problem: 'Some syllabi call this topic electronics in automotive and its evolution' is vague and sits in the middle of a technical paragraph about bus voltage, breaking the flow.
fix: Delete the sentence, or move it to the end of the section as: 'Course outlines often name this topic automotive electronics and its evolution.'

problem: The single node 'Dynamo and 12 V' merges two separate changes. Moving from 6 V to 12 V was one change; the alternator came later, as node d shows, and readers may think 12 V arrived only with the alternator.
fix: Label node c 'Dynamo, 6 V to 12 V' with note 'charging and loads', keeping node d as 'Alternator, higher output'.
